$comment: SHARED BACKEND<->FRONTEND CONTRACT. Every error_kind that can reach the
frontend on a `tool_error` SSE frame, and what the UI must do with it.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. ChatPanel's subset test proves every kind in
TOOL_ERROR_BANNER_KINDS has KIND_COPY — a kind that routes losing its
copy. It cannot see the other direction: a kind that SHOULD route and
does not. That is the direction that actually bit us, twice, and both
times the symptom was identical and silent — the banner's copy existed
and was simply unreachable, so the user got a truncated gray tool line.
`inactive_acting_user` was corrected that way, and so were
`not_authorized` and `unknown_profile_id`.
Neither side can close it alone: the backend knows what it can emit and
nothing about copy; the frontend knows its copy and cannot enumerate the
backend. So the set lives here, and both sides assert against it.
HOW IT IS ENFORCED.
backend/tests/test_tool_error_kind_manifest.py
derives the set from the source and fails if it differs from the
keys below. A NEW error_kind therefore fails the build until
somebody classifies it here.
frontend/src/components/ChatPanel.manifest.test.tsx
asserts every `banner` kind is in TOOL_ERROR_BANNER_KINDS AND in
KIND_COPY, and every `inline` kind is in neither.
THE DERIVED SET IS A SUPERSET, deliberately. It is every `error_kind`
literal yielded at a `tool_error` site, plus every one appearing in ANY
dict literal anywhere in the backend, because tool dispatch forwards any
exception carrying `detail['error_kind']` (chat_service._run_one_tool's
except block) and those details are not always written inline at the
raise — `study_in_flight` is built in `project_context.study_swap_refusal`
and raised as a variable, which an HTTPException-scoped scan missed.
Some kinds it finds are only ever raised from a route and never from a
tool handler; those are classified `inline` with that as the reason.
Over-including costs a line of JSON; under-including is the bug this file
exists to prevent.
surface: 'banner' = promote to the error banner (needs KIND_COPY).
'inline' = leave as the gray tool line.
Changing one is a UI decision. Write down why, as the entries do.

aborted.why: The user pressed stop. Announcing their own action in a banner is noise.

capability_unsupported.why: The profile cannot do what the turn needs (vision, tools). A configuration problem only the user can fix, and the turn is over. It already had KIND_COPY and did not route — the same unreachable-copy shape as inactive_acting_user.

commercial_binding_invalid.why: The commercial config cannot bind to this network (a missing Link, an unrated snapshot, ...). The model reads the message and fixes the config within the turn.

commercial_config_invalid.why: define_participants: the stored commercial config no longer validates. The model re-saves it with update_solver_config first.

confirmation_denied.why: The user denied the card. Their own decision, already visible on the card.

confirmation_expired.why: The card timed out; the action did not happen and the user must redo it.

descendants_exist.why: A destructive project operation was refused. The user chooses cascade or rename.

empty_file.why: Upload rejected. The user must supply a different file.

excel_parse_failed.why: One read failed on one workbook. The turn continues and the model reports it in prose.

file_integrity_error.why: Raised by upload_service on a stored-file checksum mismatch, reached through the upload ROUTE rather than a tool handler. Kept here because the forwarder would carry it if a tool ever did.

file_too_large.why: Upload rejected against the 25 MB cap. The user must act.

finance_inputs_invalid.why: The stored finance inputs do not validate (the route's 422 lists the errors). The model tells the user which fields; they are corrected in the Investment tab.

finance_inputs_missing.why: run_investment_case / solve_ppa_price with no stored finance inputs. The model asks the user to fill in the Investment tab; there is no chat tool that writes them.

format_not_supported.why: One tool could not read one format. Per-call, and the model can try another route.

image_analysis_timeout.why: The vision call timed out at 30 s. Nothing came back and the user should retry.

image_too_large.why: Attachment rejected against the 10 MB multimodal cap.

import_tariff_ref_conflict.why: The project's inline tariff differs from the Library item its ref names. The model explains and asks which to keep; a binding code surfaced by attach_tariff.

inactive_acting_user.why: The account stopped being active mid-turn. Nothing will work until it is fixed, and a gray tool line truncates that away — this is the correction the whole manifest generalises.

inline_tariff_would_be_replaced.why: attach_tariff refused to replace a project's inline import tariff with a different Library tariff. The model asks the user and calls again with replace_inline=true — a question it is already asking in prose.

internal_error.why: An unhandled server failure. It reaches the client on a turn-terminal `error` frame, which the banner renders directly from KIND_COPY — it is not yielded at any `tool_error` site.

invalid_base64.why: Malformed payload into one tool call. The model can correct and retry.

invalid_decision.why: A confirm request carried something other than approve/deny — a client bug, not a user-actionable state.

invalid_filename.why: Upload rejected on the filename. The user must rename.

invalid_png.why: One image failed to decode in one tool call.

invalid_tool_args.why: The model sent arguments that do not match the schema. It sees the error and retries within the turn; a banner would fire on a self-correcting step.

invalid_transcript.why: Raised by POST /chat/import validating a pasted transcript. Route-only — no tool imports transcripts.

investment_case_busy.why: run_investment_case / solve_ppa_price: a solve or a study is running (the study mesh's 409). A standing condition the model reports; the user waits for it or aborts it.

investment_case_not_solved.why: run_investment_case / solve_ppa_price before a solve (or on a stale dispatch). The model says the network must be solved first; the run needs the solved dispatch.

investment_case_refused.why: solve_ppa_price: the finance adapter refused to build the case (FinanceRefused; its `code` says why, e.g. template_not_annual). The model explains the code in prose; get_investment_case shows the same refusal for a run.

investment_case_request_invalid.why: An investment-case tool got an argument out of range (an empty owner, a page < 1, a target IRR or year outside the SolvePpa bounds). The model corrects the argument and retries, like invalid_tool_args.

library_ref_stale.why: A Library reference no longer matches its item (edited or removed). The model re-reads the Library and retries or asks; a route code surfaced by attach_tariff.

load_not_found.why: The named load is not in the network. The user gave a name that does not exist.

mime_not_allowlisted_for_multimodal.why: The file type cannot be attached; the user is told to use the read tool instead.

no_acting_user.why: No authenticated identity is bound to the turn, so every project-scoped tool 401s. Same family as inactive_acting_user and equally terminal — it was the one member of that family still unrouted.

no_active_project.why: Most tools need a project; the model recovers by asking which one, in prose, inside the same turn. Promoting it would banner a question the assistant is already asking.

no_commercial_config.why: attach_tariff needs a commercial config with a poc_link first. The model sets it (update_solver_config) and retries within the turn.

not_authorized.why: The account may not take this action (e.g. switching the instance-wide profile). Terminal for the request and needs an administrator.

parallel_destructive_not_allowed.why: Several destructive calls arrived in one turn and none ran. The user must reissue them one at a time.

profile_switch_requires_new_chat.why: The session is bound to one provider's block shapes, so a mid-session switch is refused. Emitted as an `error` frame with its own `new-chat` action; the banner already gets it without tool_error routing.

project_exists.why: A save was refused to avoid an overwrite. The user chooses rename or force.

project_lock_not_held.why: Raised by routers/projects.py when a mutation arrives without the lock — a client-sequencing bug rather than a user-actionable state.

project_lock_unavailable.why: Someone else holds the lock. Transient and usually resolves; the model reports it and can retry.

project_locked.why: Raised by the projects and solve-queue routes. Route-only today; kept classified so it cannot arrive unnoticed if a tool starts reaching it.

project_switched_mid_turn.why: DELIBERATE, and do not 'fix' it: the same guard also yields this as an `error` frame (chat_service, right after the per-tool refusals), and THAT is what reaches the banner. Promoting the tool_error copy too would show the banner twice for one event.

rate_limited_local.why: The local per-session turn limiter, raised by the chat route before a turn starts — so it never arrives on a tool_error frame in practice.

snapshot_count_mismatch.why: Supplied rows do not match the network's snapshots. The data must be corrected.

snapshot_range_mismatch.why: Supplied time range does not match the network's snapshots.

solve_ppa_ambiguous_contract.why: solve_ppa_price without contract_id on a case with several PPAs. The model asks which contract, then retries with contract_id.

solve_ppa_cash_not_established.why: solve_ppa_price: the post-tax equity cash is not established even at a zero price (a missing input). The model points to get_investment_case's reasons.

solve_ppa_contract_not_found.why: solve_ppa_price: no owner-sold PPA settlement line matches contract_id (or the case has none). The model names the contracts it knows or asks which one — within the turn.

solve_ppa_needs_redispatch.why: solve_ppa_price on a contract that changes the dispatch: a finance-only solve cannot re-dispatch (plan C9). The model explains the limit in prose.

solve_ppa_irr_ambiguous.why: solve_ppa_price: a price makes the NPV zero at the target, but the truncated equity cash has several IRRs and the engine's own (the root closest to 0) is not the target, so the price does not give the target IRR as reported (P4 gate). Its `code` carries that IRR; the model explains, nothing to fix in the UI.

solve_ppa_no_root.why: solve_ppa_price: no price in the search range reaches the target (its `code` says why, e.g. the target is met at a zero price). A finding the model reports, not a failure to route.

solve_ppa_not_linear.why: solve_ppa_price on a contract whose settlement is not linear in its price (plan C9). An answer the model explains; there is nothing for the user to fix in the UI.

solve_ppa_not_owner_sold.why: solve_ppa_price on a contract the owner buys, not sells (plan C9). The model explains that only an owner-sold PPA can be solved.

solve_ppa_price_unknown.why: solve_ppa_price on a contract whose price is not established in the case. The model says the contract needs a price first.

solver_in_flight.why: A foreground solve is running and the operation was refused. The user waits or aborts.

study_in_flight.why: An adequacy study is running and a save/queue was refused. Deliberately QUIET on the client (`QUIET_TOAST_CODES` in api/client.ts): it is a standing condition the caller handles, and one toast per autosave tick would bury the workbench.

tax_pack_not_found.why: The finance inputs name a tax pack with no version covering the financial close. The model reports it and asks for another pack or date — a question in prose.

template_refused.why: define_participants: the template cannot be built for this site (its code says why, e.g. template_needs_group_contract). The model tells the user or picks another template.

time_column_parse_error.why: The time column could not be parsed as datetimes; the user must fix the input.

too_many_multimodal_blocks.why: More than 20 attachments. The user must send fewer.

tool_call_cap_exceeded.why: The turn hit MAX_TOOL_CALLS_PER_TURN and stopped. Terminal, and the only per-turn bound there is.

tool_error.why: The forwarder's own fallback when a tool raises something with no structured error_kind. Generic by construction — there is no copy to write, which is exactly why the specific kinds beside it exist.

tool_not_offered.why: The endpoint asked for a tool that was never offered this turn. On a branch whose point is aiming the assistant at arbitrary endpoints, the user should see it.

tool_timeout.why: One tool exceeded its budget. The turn continues and the model can route around it.

turn_already_in_flight.why: A second turn arrived while one was running. Route-level, on an `error` frame, and the composer state already says so.

unknown_confirmation_token.why: A confirm arrived for a token this session does not know — a stale tab or a double-submit, not a user-actionable state.

unknown_library_kind.why: A Library tool got a kind other than tariff / contract / connection_agreement. The model corrects the argument and retries, like invalid_tool_args.

unknown_profile_id.why: The selected profile no longer exists — fires for every open chat the moment a super-admin deletes one, and C-4 made it reachable.

unknown_session.why: Raised by the chat route for a session id it does not hold. Route-only; a turn cannot be running under a session that does not exist.

unknown_step_kind.why: An internal script/step vocabulary mismatch — a bug in the caller, not a user-actionable state, and never yielded at a tool_error site.

unknown_tool.why: The model named a tool that does not exist. It sees the error and corrects within the turn, like invalid_tool_args.

unsupported_mime.why: Upload rejected on type. The user must supply something else.

upload_not_found.why: A referenced upload is gone. The user must re-attach.

upload_quota_exceeded.why: The per-project upload quota is full. The user must delete something.

urdb_invalid.why: The URDB import arguments did not validate (e.g. valid_from not a date). The model corrects and retries.

urdb_multiple_rates.why: The uploaded OpenEI response holds several rates; the error lists them and the model retries with item_index, asking the user which one if unclear.

urdb_refused.why: A URDB import refused fields by name (the route's 422). The model lists them and asks whether to import partially (accept_partial) — a question in prose, within the turn.

urdb_upload_unreadable.why: The uploaded file is not a URDB rate the importer can read (not JSON, no rates, a REopt scenario with only a label). The model says so in prose and asks for another file.

user_code_disabled.why: Raised by routers/simulation._gate_user_code on the solver-config ROUTE, never from a tool handler, so it cannot reach a tool_error frame. Listed because the derivation matches every error_kind dict literal on purpose (it under-approximated once and missed study_in_flight). Refuses extra_functionality_code when the operator has not set PYPSA_GUI_ALLOW_USER_CODE; the settings form shows the detail where the user typed the code.

user_code_forbidden.why: Same route and same reason as user_code_disabled: a config-PUT refusal, not a tool frame. Refuses a non-admin setting extra_functionality_code, which is exec()-ed in-process. Inline so the message lands next to the field; a banner would announce another user's lack of privilege in the chat surface, which is not where the attempt happened.

validation_error.why: The forwarder's Pydantic fallback. Its message is the useful part; the kind itself says only 'the arguments were wrong', which the model retries.

value_column_parse_error.why: The value column holds non-numeric data; the user must fix the input.

value_flows_changed.why: define_participants: the value-flow config changed between its read and its write (If-Match). The model reads it again and retries.

value_flows_invalid.why: define_participants: the value-flow config names a party, asset or item the project does not have (the problems are listed). The model corrects the config and retries.

value_flows_would_be_replaced.why: define_participants refused to replace (or clear) an existing, different value-flow config. The model asks the user and calls again with replace=true.

vision_call_failed.why: The vision sub-call failed outright. Nothing came back.

vision_invalid_json.why: The vision response did not parse. Nothing usable came back.
